translation: 海报；（在网络留言板上）发布消息的人
definitionEn:
(1) n. a large printed notice or picture put up in a public place to advertise or announce something
(2) n. a large printed picture or photograph stuck on a wall as decoration
(3) n. a person who posts a message on an Internet forum or message board

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （网络论坛、留言板上的）发帖人
uncommonMeanings.example: The anonymous poster first shared the missing boy's photo. 那位匿名发帖人最先分享了走失男孩的照片。

readingExamples: Make posters and put them up around the school;

posExamples.sentence: Under the flickering streetlamp, Amy smoothed out the hand-drawn poster of her lost cat, pressed it against the cold wall, and whispered a small prayer before hurrying to the next corner. （读后续写·寻宠·动作细节）
Eye-catching posters will be put up at the school gate and in every classroom next Monday, so please take a moment to read them for further details about the charity sale. （应用文·活动通知）
A well-designed poster can convey an environmental message at a single glance, which explains why visual campaigns often reach audiences that lengthy articles fail to touch. （议论文·宣传方式）

wordForms.noun: post（帖子；邮件；职位）；poster（海报；发帖人）
wordForms.other: 构词法·后缀 -er：post（张贴/发布）+ -er → poster，字面"张贴之物→海报"，或"发布的人→发帖人"。同一 -er 兼指"物"与"人"，靠语境区分。put up posters = 张贴海报（put up 为高频短语）。复数直接加 -s：posters。

idioms.idiom: a poster child / poster boy / poster girl (for sth)
idioms.example: Once a struggling stutterer, the young speaker has become a poster child for what determination and daily practice can achieve. （议论文·励志论据）

collocations.phrase: make posters and put them up
collocations.translation: 制作并张贴海报（课文原句词块）
collocations.example: Make posters and put them up around the school. 制作海报并张贴在校园各处。（课文原句）

collocations.phrase: put up / stick up a poster
collocations.example: Volunteers put up posters along the main street. 志愿者们沿主街张贴海报。
Each class is invited to design a poster on saving water. 邀请各班设计一张节水海报。
He refused to take down the poster after the concert. 演唱会结束后他也不肯取下那张海报。

collocations.translation: 醒目的/色彩鲜艳的海报
collocations.example: An eye-catching poster at the gate will attract more visitors. 门口一张醒目的海报会吸引更多人。
On the board hung a poster advertising the English Corner. 布告栏上挂着一张宣传英语角的海报。
The faded movie poster on his bedroom wall told everyone what the quiet boy dreamed of becoming. （读后续写·环境暗示人物）
The student union launched a poster campaign against food waste, and within weeks the leftover trays in the canteen had visibly shrunk. （议论文·事例论证）

synonyms.example: A notice on the board says the library will extend its opening hours during the final exam weeks. （应用文·通知）
synonyms.usage: 侧重传达文字信息的告示;poster 强调图文并茂、有视觉冲击力的宣传画

synonyms.example: The marathon route was lined with cheering families holding hand-made placards of encouragement. （读后续写·赛事场面）
synonyms.usage: 多指手举或竖立的标语牌,常见于集会、比赛现场;poster 通常张贴于墙面

synonyms.example: Volunteers handed out flyers about the blood donation drive at the school gate during lunch break. （应用文·活动报道）
synonyms.usage: 指发到人手中的单页宣传品,小而便携;poster 尺寸大、固定张贴、供远观

advancedExpressions.expression: make / design a poster｜put up posters｜take down a poster｜an eye-catching poster｜a poster advertising sth｜a poster campaign
advancedExpressions.example: Make posters and put them up around the school. 制作海报并张贴在校园各处。（课文句式）

advancedExpressions.expression: post（v. 张贴/发布）+ -er →（物）poster 海报／（人）poster 发帖人；类比：teach+er 老师，contain+er 容器
advancedExpressions.example: The poster put up on the board and the poster who posted online share one root: post. 布告栏上的海报与网上的发帖人同根 post。

advancedExpressions.expression: ..., plastered with posters of ..., betrayed ...
advancedExpressions.example: The bedroom wall, plastered with posters of distant galaxies, betrayed the quiet dream the boy had never dared to say aloud. （以环境细节暗示人物内心）

advancedExpressions.expression: As is vividly shown on the poster, ...
advancedExpressions.example: As is vividly shown on the poster, the English Festival will feature drama, debate and dubbing contests. （as 引导非限制性定语从句）

advancedExpressions.expression: No poster, however striking, can substitute for ...
advancedExpressions.example: No poster, however striking, can substitute for genuine action; awareness raised on paper must eventually walk off the wall and into our daily lives. （否定主语+however 让步插入语+隐喻,深化论证）

sentenceUpgrade.original: We made posters and put them up around the school.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Armed with brushes and boundless enthusiasm, we spent the whole afternoon painting posters, and by dusk our colourful invitations were smiling from every wall and notice board on campus. （读后续写·活动筹备）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: Armed with ... 过去分词开头 + 拟人(invitations were smiling) + 时间推进(by dusk)营造画面感

sentenceUpgrade.original: The poster gives information about the club.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Displayed prominently at the school entrance, the poster offers a clear picture of the club's aims, weekly activities and application procedure, ensuring that no interested student misses the chance to join. （应用文·招募说明）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 过去分词短语开头(Displayed ...) + 三项并列名词结构 + ensuring 现在分词表结果

original_sentence: Make posters and put them up around the school;

classPractice.question: To attract more students, we will make posters and ____ ____ ____ around the school. (把它们张贴起来)
classPractice.note: 还原课文原句 make posters and put them up；put up = 张贴，代词 them 置于 put 与 up 之间。

classPractice.question: Eye-catching ____ (poster) will be put up at the school gate next Monday.
classPractice.note: 海报是可数名词，此处泛指多张，用复数 posters；谓语 will be put up 为被动。

classPractice.question: Volunteers handed out ____ (posters / flyers) to passers-by, while big ____ were stuck on the walls for people to read from a distance.
classPractice.note: 发到人手里的小传单是 flyers；张贴墙上供远观的大幅宣传画是 posters。

definitionEn:
(1) adj. connected with education for children between the ages of 11 and 18
(2) adj. less important than something else
(3) adj. happening as a result of something else

uncommonMeanings.meaning: ①次要的，从属的（less important，与 primary"首要的"相对）
uncommonMeanings.example: Winning is secondary; taking part is what counts. 输赢是次要的，参与才重要。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: ②继发的，次生的（happening as a result；医学/科学）
uncommonMeanings.example: The doctors feared the secondary complications. 医生们担心继发的并发症。

readingExamples: I had the chance to study at a British secondary school as an exchange student.
Every secondary school student in the UK must study English, Maths and the Science subjects: Biology, Chemistry and Physics.

posExamples.sentence: Her secondary school years were not the best years of her life — as the cliché promised — but they were the years that shaped her, the years when she learned that popularity was a currency that could be devalued overnight and that the friends worth having were the ones who stayed when the currency crashed. （读后续写·中学生涯·社交真相）

The details of the budget were, in her view, secondary to the vision — but her colleague, a man who had seen too many beautiful visions collapse under the weight of unexamined spreadsheets, gently insisted that the secondary was precisely what made the primary possible. （读后续写·理想与现实·张力）

While academic excellence is our primary goal, we also place great emphasis on secondary but equally important aspects of education — character development, social responsibility, and the cultivation of a lifelong love for learning. （应用文·学校介绍/教育理念）

wordForms.other: 构词法·second + -ary（形容词后缀，表"属于……的"）→ secondary。词族：second 第二/秒 → secondary 中学的·次要的 → secondly 其次。对举记忆：primary（第一/小学/首要）↔ secondary（第二/中学/次要）。固定搭配 be secondary to sth（次于……），介词用 to 不用 than。

idioms.example: For her, fame was entirely secondary to the work itself — a byproduct she tolerated rather than a goal she pursued — and this, perhaps more than any talent she possessed, was the secret to her longevity in a field where most burned bright and burned out. （读后续写·艺术家品格·纯粹）

collocations.example: I had the chance to study at a British secondary school as an exchange student. 我有机会作为交换生在一所英国中学学习。（课文原句）

collocations.translation: 每一名中学生（课文原句词块）
collocations.example: Every secondary school student in the UK must study English, Maths and the Science subjects. 英国每名中学生都必须学英语、数学和理科。（课文原句）
Access to secondary education transformed the village. 接受中等教育的机会改变了这个村庄。
For her, money was secondary to happiness. 对她来说，钱不如幸福重要。
The decoration was of secondary importance. 装饰是次要的。

Her research relied heavily on secondary sources — books about books, analyses of analyses — until her professor challenged her to find one primary document, one letter written by an actual person who had lived through the event. That document, yellowed and fragile, changed everything. （读后续写·学术突破·一手资料的震撼）

synonyms.example: Children attend primary school before secondary school. 孩子先上小学，再上中学。
synonyms.usage: 教育阶段：primary school 小学（约6-11岁）→ secondary school 中学（约11-18岁）；重要程度：primary 首要的 ↔ secondary 次要的。两义都与 secondary 恰成对照，是高考高频对举。

synonyms.example: It was only a minor problem. 那只是个小问题。
synonyms.usage: minor 强调规模/程度"小"；secondary 强调层级/顺序上"居次"。作定语位置相同，但侧重不同：a minor issue（小问题）/ a secondary issue（次要问题）。

synonyms.example: She played a subordinate role in the project. 她在项目中处于从属地位。
synonyms.usage: 强调组织/结构层级中的"从属地位"，较 formal，常 be subordinate to sb/sth；secondary 更口语常用、语义更泛。

advancedExpressions.expression: secondary school｜secondary education｜be secondary to sth｜of secondary importance｜secondary source（二手资料）
advancedExpressions.example: I studied at a British secondary school as an exchange student. 我作为交换生在英国一所中学学习。（课文句式）

advancedExpressions.type: 同义表达群·功能（"次要/不如……重要"）
advancedExpressions.expression: be secondary to｜be less important than｜take second place to｜matter less than｜come after（可替换表达枚举，不辨析）
advancedExpressions.example: In her eyes, fame took second place to the work itself. 在她眼里，名声比作品本身次要。

advancedExpressions.expression: primary school 小学 ↔ secondary school 中学；primary 首要的 ↔ secondary 次要的；相关：second → secondary → secondly
advancedExpressions.example: Safety is our primary concern; all else is secondary. 安全是我们的首要关切，其余都是次要的。

advancedExpressions.expression: our primary concern is ...; all other considerations are secondary
advancedExpressions.example: Our primary concern is students' safety; all other considerations are secondary. （安全第一的层级表述）

advancedExpressions.expression: in the grand scheme of things, ... was secondary; what mattered was ...
advancedExpressions.example: In the grand scheme of things, the grade was secondary — a letter on a page, a number in a system — but what mattered, what would stay with her long after the transcript was forgotten, was the teacher who had looked at her struggling and said, not 'try harder' but 'try differently.' （成绩→一位老师的理解→终身影响）

sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Grades, I have come to believe, are secondary — not unimportant, not irrelevant, but secondary — to something far more enduring: the quality of curiosity that a student carries out of the classroom and into the rest of their life. A grade measures what you knew on a particular Tuesday in a particular room under particular conditions that may never be replicated. But curiosity — that restless, inconvenient, beautiful hunger to understand — measures something else entirely. It measures not what you have learned but what you are capable of learning, and the distance between those two things is the distance between a student who will stop at the edge of the syllabus and one who will keep walking long after the bell has rung. （读后续写/应用文·演讲·成绩vs好奇）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 让步界定(not unimportant, not irrelevant, but secondary) + 对比(grade measures what you knew vs curiosity measures what you're capable of learning) + 空间隐喻(distance between edge of syllabus and continuing to walk)

sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: This is more than a secondary school. It is, if you will permit me a moment of sentiment, a garden of second chances — a place where the child who struggled in primary finds a teacher who speaks their language, where the quiet one discovers a voice in the debate club, where the one who never quite fit in finds, in the sprawling, chaotic, magnificent ecosystem of secondary education, their people. It is called 'secondary' because it follows primary in the sequence of schooling, but let no one tell you that makes it secondary in importance. For it is here, in these four brief years between childhood and the world, that the foundations of a life are either laid well or laid poorly — and the difference between the two is everything. （应用文·学校介绍/开学演讲·重新定义「secondary」）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 多重否定矫正(not unimportant...but secondary→it is called secondary because...) + 花园隐喻(garden of second chances) + 排比the child who...the quiet one...the one who... + 对比收束(laid well or laid poorly→the difference is everything)

original_sentence: I had the chance to study at a British secondary school as an exchange student.

classPractice.question: Every ____ (second) school student in the UK must study English, Maths and the Science subjects.
classPractice.note: 还原课文原句：修饰 school 需形容词 secondary"中学的"；second 是"第二/秒"，语义不合。

classPractice.question: Children first go to ____ (primary / secondary) school, and then move on to ____ school at about the age of eleven.
classPractice.note: 教育阶段对举：primary school 小学在前，secondary school 中学在后（约11岁起）。

classPractice.question: 对她来说，赢得比赛不如享受过程重要。For her, winning the game ____ ____ ____ enjoying the process. (用 be secondary to)
classPractice.note: 固定搭配 be secondary to sth"次于/不如……重要"，介词用 to，不能用 than。

definitionEn:
(1) n. an act of giving something to somebody and receiving something in return
(2) n. an arrangement when two people or groups from different countries visit each other's homes or do each other's jobs for a short time
(3) vt. to give something to somebody and receive something in return

uncommonMeanings.meaning: ①交流；（两国间的）交换互访
uncommonMeanings.example: The two schools have a regular exchange. 两校之间有定期的交流互访。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: ②兑换；外汇（foreign exchange 外汇，高考熟词僻义）

posExamples.sentence: The exchange of letters between the two soldiers — one British, one German, stationed on opposite sides of the same frozen field — began with suspicion and ended, two winters later, with a friendship that outlasted the war and, in its small way, redeemed something that the war had tried to destroy. （读后续写·战争中的通信友谊·人性光辉）

They exchanged glances across the crowded room — not the quick, casual glance of strangers but the kind of look that contained an entire conversation, a language developed over years that required no words and tolerated no translation. （读后续写·眼神交流·默契）
I am writing to express my sincere interest in the student exchange program, which I believe would offer an invaluable opportunity for cultural immersion and personal growth. （应用文·申请信/动机信）

wordForms.other: 构词法·前缀 ex-（出）+ change（改变/换）→ exchange，字面"换出去/互相换"。名动同形，重音均在后：/ɪksˈtʃeɪndʒ/。关键搭配区别：exchange A for B（用A换B，动词）↔ in exchange for B（作为对B的交换，名词短语）。an exchange student 是复合名词（交换生）。

idioms.example: She offered her silence in exchange for nothing — not money, not favors, not even gratitude — because some secrets, she had decided, were not currency to be traded but burdens to be carried, and she had strong shoulders. （读后续写·沉默的代价·道德选择）

The organization aims for the free exchange of ideas among universities. 该组织着力于大学间思想的自由交流。（课件例句）
The meeting encouraged a lively exchange of information and opinions. 这次会议促成了信息与想法的热烈交流。
May I exchange seats with you? 我和你调一个座位好吗？（课件例句）

collocations.translation: 【课件】更换，兑换；用某物换某物
collocations.example: He gave me an apple in exchange for a cake. 他给我一个苹果，换一块蛋糕。（课件例句）
I had the chance to study at a British secondary school as an exchange student. 我有机会作为交换生在一所英国中学学习。（课文原句）

I applied for the student exchange program. 我申请了学生交换项目。

synonyms.example: They swapped lunches every day. 他们每天互换午餐。
synonyms.usage: 更口语，强调对等、随意地互换实物（swap sth for sth / swap sth with sb），日常场景多用；exchange 更正式，且能搭 ideas/views 等抽象名词。

synonyms.translation: 交易，交换（常含商业色彩）
synonyms.example: He traded his watch for a train ticket. 他用手表换了张火车票。
synonyms.usage: 强调交换有价值之物、常带商业/实用色彩（trade sth for sth）；exchange 语义更广，可指交流、互访、兑换等，商业味较淡。

advancedExpressions.expression: an exchange student｜exchange sth for sth｜in exchange (for)｜exchange ideas / views｜cultural exchange｜foreign exchange（外汇）
advancedExpressions.example: I studied there as an exchange student. 我作为交换生在那里学习。（课文句式）

advancedExpressions.type: 同义表达群·功能（"交换/互给"）
advancedExpressions.expression: exchange A for B｜swap A for B｜trade A for B｜give ... and receive ... in return｜barter（可替换表达枚举，不辨析）
advancedExpressions.example: He traded his watch for a ticket, giving up much and receiving little in return. 他用手表换了张票，付出许多而所得甚微。

advancedExpressions.type: 语法点·as 引导身份状语（从课文句长出）
advancedExpressions.expression: study ... as an exchange student —— as + 名词表"以……身份"
advancedExpressions.example: She went to Japan as an exchange student and learned to see her own country differently. 她作为交换生去日本，学会了以不同眼光看待自己的国家。（原句 as an exchange student 即身份状语）

advancedExpressions.expression: I see this as an exchange from which both sides stand to gain
advancedExpressions.example: I see this as an exchange from which both sides stand to gain — you bring resources, we bring ideas. （合作提案）

advancedExpressions.expression: an exchange that went far beyond words — it was ...
advancedExpressions.example: What followed was an exchange that went far beyond words — a trading of silences, a barter of memories. （敌人→理解→和平）

sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: They exchanged gifts on the last night of the exchange program — gifts that cost nothing in any currency but were, to each of them, priceless. She gave him a seashell from the beach where she had walked every morning of her childhood; he gave her a pebble from the river behind his grandmother's house. Two ordinary objects, indistinguishable from millions of others like them — except that each carried, in its silent mineral memory, the sound of waves and the rush of water and the unspoken promise that they would remember each other, not in the abstract way we remember acquaintances, but the way we remember a place we called home for a brief, beautiful season that changed the shape of who we were. （读后续写·交换礼物·物的情感载体·离别）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 对比(ordinary objects indistinguishable from millions vs each carried...) + 拟人(silent mineral memory) + 感官描写(sound of waves, rush of water) + 收束定调(changed the shape of who we were)

sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: If you take nothing else from this assembly, take this: a student exchange is not a holiday with homework. It is not tourism with a textbook. It is the most radical act of education I know — because it takes a student out of the only world they have ever known and places them, gently but firmly, into someone else's. It is one thing to read about another culture in a classroom; it is another thing entirely to sit at that culture's dinner table, to be the only person in the room who does not understand the joke, to stumble through a language and discover that a smile needs no translation. And in that stumbling, in that discomfort, in that beautiful, terrifying vulnerability — that is where learning happens. Not the learning that fills in bubbles on a test, but the learning that reshapes the person holding the pencil. （应用文·演讲·交换生的真正价值）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 否定定义(is not..., is not...) + 对比逐层(one thing to read...another thing to sit at the dinner table) + 排比修辞(in that stumbling, in that discomfort, in that...vulnerability) + 对比收束(not learning that fills bubbles but learning that reshapes the person)

translation: n. 主人；东道主；主持人 | vt. 主办；主持
definitionEn:
(1) n. a person who invites guests to a meal, a party, etc. and looks after them
(2) n. a country, city or organization that arranges and provides the facilities for a special event
(3) n. a person who introduces guests and performers on a television or radio programme
(4) vt. to organize an event and invite people to it; to act as the host of a place, event or programme

uncommonMeanings.example: Standing at the crossroads of graduation, she found a host of memories flooding back — the morning readings, the shared umbrellas, the whispered jokes in the back row. （读后续写·毕业·回忆蒙太奇）

idioms.example: Volunteering at the nursing home brought me a whole host of unexpected rewards, the greatest of which was learning to listen with patience. （应用文·活动感悟）

definitionEn:

(2) n. the scientific processes and features of a particular living thing or group of living things (the biology of sth)
(3) n. the physical processes that happen inside the body, as opposed to the mind

Breakthroughs in molecular biology have made it possible to treat diseases that were considered incurable only a decade ago. （议论文·科技进步）
What began as an ordinary biology lesson turned unforgettable when our teacher brought in a real beehive and let us listen to its steady, drowsy hum. （读后续写·课堂惊喜）
Please note that all students must wear gloves and follow the safety instructions strictly during the biology experiment scheduled for next Monday. （应用文·实验室通知）
Armed with a degree in biology and years of field experience, Dr. Lin has become a leading voice in the campaign to save the snow leopard. （议论文·人物例证）

synonyms.example: Advances in the life sciences are quietly reshaping medicine, agriculture and even the way we understand ourselves. （议论文·科技话题）
synonyms.usage: 更宽泛的学科统称,涵盖生物学、医学、生态学等;biology 特指"生物学"这门课程或学科,日常校园语境用 biology

advancedExpressions.expression: -logy = “……学”：biology 生物学 / geology 地质学 / psychology 心理学 / zoology 动物学 / geography 地理（-graphy）｜学者用 -logist：biologist / geologist / psychologist｜形容词用 -logical：biological / geological / psychological
advancedExpressions.example: She loves biology, but her brother prefers geology and their mother teaches psychology — three -logy subjects under one roof. 她爱生物，弟弟偏爱地质，母亲教心理学——一家三口三门“-学”。（一句巩固学科词族）

advancedExpressions.expression: Designed for students who ..., the biology course/club offers ...
advancedExpressions.example: Designed for students who are endlessly curious about the living world, the biology club offers hands-on experiments, field trips and the rare joy of watching textbook knowledge come alive. （过去分词短语开头+三项并列,招新启事高分框架）

advancedExpressions.expression: A solid grounding in ... not only ... but also ...
advancedExpressions.example: A solid grounding in biology not only sharpens our scientific reasoning but also teaches us humility before the astonishing complexity of nature. （not only...but also 递进论证+抽象名词升格）

sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Of all the subjects on my timetable, it is biology that never fails to set my curiosity alight, for every slide under the microscope seems to whisper a small secret about how life works. （夹叙夹议·兴趣描写）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: Of all... 范围铺垫 + it is...that 强调句 + never fails to 双重否定强化 + 拟人(whisper a secret)

original_sentence: Every secondary school student in the UK must study English, Maths and the Science subjects: Biology, Chemistry and Physics.

classPractice.question: 在英国，每个中学生都必须学习英语、数学以及生物、化学、物理这些科学科目。Every secondary school student in the UK must study English, Maths and the Science subjects: ____ (生物), Chemistry and Physics.
classPractice.note: 课文原句；学科名 biology 首字母大写作专有科目名，不可数、不加冠词

classPractice.question: Inspired by her volunteer work, Mei decided to major in biology and become a ____ (biology).
classPractice.note: 学科 -logy → 学者 -logist；biology→biologist 生物学家

classPractice.question: The study of the earth's rocks is called ge____, just as the study of living things is called biology.
classPractice.note: -logy 表'……学'；geology 地质学，与 biology 同构词法

translation: 艰难的；严厉的；坚强的；坚固的
definitionEn:
(1) adj. difficult to do or deal with
(2) adj. demanding that particular rules be obeyed and showing a lack of sympathy
(3) adj. strong enough to deal with difficult conditions or situations

uncommonMeanings.meaning: ①（肉等）嚼不动的，老的（熟词僻义，反义 tender 嫩的）
uncommonMeanings.example: The steak was too tough to cut, let alone chew. 这块牛排太老了，切都切不动，更别提嚼了。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: ②（人）坚强的，能吃苦的，强硬的（tough on sb 对某人严厉）
uncommonMeanings.example: Years of hardship had made her tough enough to face anything. 多年的艰辛已把她磨炼得足以面对任何事。

readingExamples: In the beginning, however, it was still tough for me to remember everyone's name!

posExamples.sentence: The first year after her mother left was the toughest — a year measured not in months but in meals cooked alone, in mornings when getting out of bed felt like an athletic event, in the thousand small silences where a voice used to be. But she survived it, and in surviving, she discovered a toughness she had not known she possessed. （读后续写·艰难岁月·发现内在力量）

The coach was tough — not cruel, never cruel, but demanding in a way that made you discover capabilities you would have sworn you did not have — and years later, his former players would say that the toughness he taught them on the field was the toughness that got them through everything that came after. （读后续写·严厉的教练·终身受益）

I have to make a tough decision regarding the upcoming event, and I would greatly appreciate your honest advice — because the toughest decisions are the ones we should never make alone. （应用文·求助信/征求意见）

wordForms.other: 小贴士：tough /tʌf/ 中 -ough 读 /ʌf/，与 rough、enough 同类；勿与 though /ðəʊ/、through /θruː/、thought /θɔːt/ 混淆——同为 -ough 拼写却读音各异，是易错拼读群。形容词加 -en 变使役动词：toughen 使坚韧

idioms.idiom: when the going gets tough, the tough get going
idioms.translation: 艰难时刻方显英雄本色
idioms.example: When the going got tough — and it got very tough, with funding cut and half the team gone and a deadline that seemed to be approaching at twice the normal speed — the tough got going, not with dramatic speeches but with quiet, unglamorous persistence, the kind that wakes up early and stays late and does the work that no one will ever applaud. （读后续写·逆境坚持·不为人知的奋斗）

idioms.translation: 难对付的人/难解决的问题
idioms.example: The old librarian was a tough nut to crack — she had not smiled at a student in thirty years, if the legends were to be believed — but the new girl, with her patient questions and her habit of returning books two days early, somehow found a crack in the shell, and what emerged was not a smile exactly, but something close enough. （读后续写·打开心扉·温暖）

collocations.translation: 【课件】困难的，难做的（a tough childhood 苦难的童年 / a tough decision 很难的决定 / a tough time 艰难时期）
collocations.example: It's a tough decision to make. 那是个很难做的决定。／ The family has had a tough time (of it) during the last few months. 这家人过去几个月过得很艰难。（课件例句）

collocations.phrase: it is tough for sb to do sth
collocations.translation: 【课件】对某人来说做某事很艰难（it 作形式主语）
collocations.example: It is tough for her to achieve/strike a balance between work and family. 对她来说，平衡工作和家庭是很艰难的。（课件例句）

collocations.phrase: tough = strict; be tough on sb; talk tough
collocations.translation: 【课件】严厉的；对某人严厉；说话强硬
collocations.example: Don't be too tough on her—she was just trying to help. 别对她这么严厉，她只是想帮忙而已。（课件例句）

collocations.phrase: tough = strong 坚强的；a tough guy
collocations.translation: 【课件】坚强的，健壮的，能吃苦耐劳的；硬汉
collocations.example: He plays a tough guy in the movie. 他在电影里演一个硬汉。／ He is not tough enough for a career in sales. 他干推销这一行缺少足够的韧劲。（课件例句）

collocations.translation: 【课件】韧性、强健、坚强／使坚韧、变坚强
collocations.example: She has toughened (up) a lot since her mother died. 母亲去世之后，她坚强了很多。（课件例句）

She faced the toughest decision of her life at seventeen — stay with the family that needed her or take the scholarship that would change everything — and the fact that neither choice was wrong made the choosing infinitely harder. （读后续写·两难选择·成长的代价）

Her grandmother practiced a kind of tough love that the modern world had almost forgotten — not the toughness of cruelty but the toughness of high expectations, the toughness that refused to let you settle for less than you were capable of. （读后续写·长辈的爱·严格即关怀）

synonyms.example: It was a difficult / tough decision, and she lay awake all night weighing it. 这是个艰难的决定，她整夜辗转难眠地权衡。
synonyms.usage: 辨析：difficult 最中性、最通用，指“需要努力才能完成/理解”，可修饰任务、问题、人；tough 更口语、语气更重，强调“棘手、难熬、需要毅力去扛”，还可指(局势)严峻、(人)坚韧、(肉)老。‘一个艰难的决定’两者皆可，但 tough decision 更有“咬牙硬扛”的味道

synonyms.translation: 有韧性的，能迅速恢复的
synonyms.example: She was the most resilient person he had ever met — life had knocked her down so many times it was almost a ritual, and every time she got back up, not unbruised, not unbroken, but standing, always standing, with a look in her eyes that said, 'Is that all you've got?' （读后续写·百折不挠·生命力）
synonyms.usage: 强调弹性和恢复力，比tough更侧重反弹而非硬扛

synonyms.example: The course was demanding in a way that first-year students found almost offensive — as if the professor had forgotten that they were beginners, as if he expected them to think like experts before they had learned the basics — but by the end of the semester, they realized that his demands had been a kind of respect. （读后续写·高要求的老师·尊重的另一面）
synonyms.usage: 侧重对他人要求严格，tough也可形容局势艰难

advancedExpressions.type: 语法点·tough 一词多义（课件）
advancedExpressions.expression: tough = difficult 艰难的 ｜ tough = strict 严厉的（be tough on sb）｜ tough = strong 坚强的、能吃苦的（a tough guy）；派生 toughness n. 韧性 / toughen v. 使坚韧
advancedExpressions.example: It was a tough childhood, but hardship toughened him, and today he is known as a tough negotiator no one dares to be tough on. 那是苦难的童年，但艰辛磨炼了他，如今他是无人敢对之强硬的强硬谈判者。（课件三义贯通）

advancedExpressions.expression: a tough decision / choice 艰难的决定 / a tough time 艰难时期 / tough love 严厉的爱 / be tough on sb 对某人严厉 / tough it out 咬牙挺过去 / a tough nut to crack 难对付的人(事)
advancedExpressions.example: It was a tough time, but she chose to tough it out rather than give up. 那是段艰难的日子，但她选择咬牙挺过去而非放弃。（tough time + tough it out 连用）

advancedExpressions.expression: tough times did not break sb.; they revealed who sb. truly was
advancedExpressions.example: The tough times — and there were many, more than any one person should have to endure — did not break her; they revealed her. As heat reveals the quality of metal and pressure reveals the integrity of stone, adversity revealed in her a core of something unyielding, something that bent but never broke, something that the easy years, had they continued, would have left undiscovered and unnamed. （逆境如熔炉→揭示真我→金属与石头的比喻）

advancedExpressions.expression: I don't want to sugarcoat this — it is going to be tough, but ...
advancedExpressions.example: I don't want to sugarcoat this — the next phase is going to be tough. The workload will increase, the expectations will rise, and there will be moments when you question whether you made the right choice. But here is what I can promise: if you push through the tough part, what waits on the other side is worth every difficult moment. （坦诚的领导者/导师话语）

sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: It was a tough time — not the cinematic kind of tough, with dramatic music and a triumphant ending, but the quiet, grinding tough of everyday survival. The tough of counting coins at the grocery store, of patching shoes because new ones were a luxury, of smiling at a child who asked for things you could not provide and inventing reasons that did not involve the word 'poverty.' But here is what the tough times taught her, and it is a lesson she would not trade for an easier childhood: toughness is not the absence of vulnerability. It is not a wall you build to keep pain out. Toughness, real toughness, is the willingness to feel the full weight of a difficult life and still, somehow, despite everything, to get up in the morning and try again. （读后续写·重新定义「tough」·日常的艰难与真正的坚韧）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 否定定义(not cinematic tough but quiet grinding tough) + 具象化(the tough of counting coins, patching shoes, smiling) + 核心重定(toughness is not absence of vulnerability...it is the willingness to feel and still try)

sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: People will tell you to be tough — as if toughness were a switch you could flip, a mask you could put on. But let me offer a different kind of advice: don't try to be tough. Try instead to be flexible. The tree that refuses to bend in the storm is the tree that breaks; the reed that bows to the wind is the one still standing when the sky clears. Resilience — the ability to bend without breaking, to absorb without shattering — that is the toughness that lasts. So don't harden yourself against the world; soften yourself into someone the world cannot break. （应用文·演讲·重新定义坚强·芦苇vs大树）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 反驳引入(People will tell you...But let me offer...) + 经典比喻(tree vs reed/伊索寓言) + 悖论收束(soften yourself into someone the world cannot break)

original_sentence: In the beginning, however, it was still tough for me to remember everyone's name!

classPractice.question: 对她来说，平衡工作和家庭是很艰难的。（用 tough）
classPractice.answer: It is tough for her to achieve / strike a balance between work and family.
classPractice.note: 课件原题。it is tough for sb to do sth 结构；achieve/strike a balance between A and B 在 A 与 B 之间取得平衡。

classPractice.question: 起初，要记住每个人的名字对我来说仍然很难。In the beginning, however, it was still ____ for me to remember everyone's name.
classPractice.note: 课文原句；it was tough (for sb) to do sth 做某事很难，it 作形式主语

classPractice.question: The meat was overcooked and far too ____ (tough / difficult) to chew.
classPractice.note: 形容（肉）老、嚼不动只能用 tough，difficult 不修饰食物质地

classPractice.question: Facing a ____ (tough) decision, she turned to her mentor, whose calm ____ (tough) always steadied her.
classPractice.note: 前空作定语用形容词 tough；后空作名词'坚韧'用 toughness

translation: n. 闹钟；恐慌；警报；警报器 | vt. 使惊恐，使害怕
definitionEn:
(1) n. a loud noise that warns people of danger
(2) n. a feeling of fear or worry
(3) n. a device that wakes you up
(4) vt. to make somebody feel frightened or worried

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 【课件】惊恐，惊慌（不可数；in alarm 惊慌地；a growing sense of alarm 越来越强的惊慌感）
uncommonMeanings.example: She looked around in alarm. 她惊慌地环顾四周。（课件例句）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 【课件】使惊恐，使担忧（alarm sb；常用被动 be alarmed by / at sth）
uncommonMeanings.example: She was alarmed by/at the thought of going back home alone. 一想到独自回家，她就害怕。（课件例句）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: ①惊恐，担忧（不可数，in alarm 惊恐地；with alarm 担忧地）
uncommonMeanings.example: She looked up in alarm as the lights suddenly went out. 灯突然熄灭，她惊恐地抬起头。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: ②使惊恐，使担忧（常用被动 be alarmed at/by sth）
uncommonMeanings.example: I don't want to alarm you, but the door was left open all night. 我不想吓你，但门整晚都开着。

readingExamples: I like it so much that I still use it as my alarm!

posExamples.sentence: The alarm went off at five — as it had every morning for the past two years — and in the darkness before dawn, with the world still asleep and the weight of another day pressing against her chest, she gave herself exactly sixty seconds to feel sorry for herself, and then she got up. Because self-pity, she had learned, was a luxury, and luxuries were for people who had someone else to set their alarm. （读后续写·艰辛生活·自立的重量）

A flicker of alarm crossed her face — so brief that anyone not paying attention would have missed it — but he saw it, and in that fraction of a second, he understood that the situation was far more serious than anyone had let on. （读后续写·微妙情绪·危机暗示）
I don't wish to alarm anyone, but the fire exit on the third floor appears to be blocked, and I believe this warrants immediate attention before it becomes a genuine emergency. （应用文·报告问题·冷静提醒）

wordForms.adjective: alarming（令人担忧的） / alarmed（感到担忧的）
wordForms.other: 小贴士：情感形容词一对——alarming 修饰事物“令人担忧的”（an alarming rate 惊人的速度），alarmed 修饰人“感到担忧的”（be/feel alarmed）；同类还有 alarmist 危言耸听者。alarm 既是名词又是动词，同形

idioms.example: It was the youngest member of the team — the intern, of all people — who first raised the alarm about the structural flaw that everyone else had overlooked, and in doing so, she taught the entire engineering firm a lesson about the value of fresh eyes. （读后续写·新人发现危机·初生牛犊）

The fire turned out to be a false alarm — a faulty sensor, the fire chief explained with barely concealed irritation — but for the twenty minutes before that announcement, the entire building had stood on the pavement in various states of undress and disarray, and in that strange, suspended moment, strangers had spoken to each other, had offered jackets and reassurance, had been, briefly, a community. （读后续写·虚惊一场·意外的人性温暖）

collocations.phrase: set the alarm (for) / an alarm clock
collocations.example: I set my alarm for 6.30 a.m. before going to bed. 睡前我把闹钟设在早上6点半。（课件例句）
She decided to sound/raise the alarm. 她决定发出警报。（课件例句）

collocations.phrase: set off / activate / trigger the alarm
collocations.example: The cat set off/activated/triggered the alarm. 猫触动了警报。（课件例句）

collocations.phrase: the alarm goes off / sounds / rings
collocations.example: A car alarm went off/sounded/rang in the middle of the night. 半夜里汽车警报响了。（课件例句）

collocations.phrase: in alarm; a growing sense of alarm
collocations.translation: 【课件】惊恐地；越来越强的惊慌感（n. 惊恐，惊慌）
collocations.example: She looked around in alarm. 她惊慌地环顾四周。／ I felt a growing sense of alarm when he didn't return that night. 那晚他没回来，我越来越感到惊慌。（课件例句）

collocations.phrase: alarm sb; be alarmed by / at sth
collocations.translation: 【课件】(v.) 使某人惊恐、担忧；因……而害怕、惊恐
collocations.example: The mother didn't want to alarm her child. 妈妈不想让孩子害怕。／ She was alarmed by/at the thought of going back home alone. 一想到独自回家，她就害怕。（课件例句）

collocations.translation: 【课件】令人惊慌的（修饰事物）／感到惊慌的（修饰人）／惊人地
collocations.example: The Amazon rainforest is disappearing at an alarming speed. 亚马逊热带雨林正在以惊人的速度消失。／ During the early 19th century the crime rate rose alarmingly. 在19世纪初，犯罪率惊人地上升。（课件例句）

She set her alarm for four — an hour earlier than usual — because the exam was at eight and she wanted time to review, to breathe, to sit with her anxiety until it became manageable rather than overwhelming. （读后续写·考前准备·紧张管理）

The sudden drop in test scores caused alarm among the faculty — not because numbers mattered more than students but because numbers, when they change dramatically, are often the first sign of a deeper problem that has not yet learned to speak in words. （应用文·数据分析/读后续写·教育反思）

She turned in alarm at the sound of shattering glass — and found her little brother standing in a puddle of what had been, moments ago, their mother's favorite vase, his face a war between terror and the desperate hope that this was somehow not his fault. （读后续写·童年闯祸·鲜活场景）

collocations.phrase: the alarm goes off / rings / sounds
collocations.example: The alarm went off at half past six, its insistent beeping slicing through a dream she was already forgetting — something about a train station and a ticket she couldn't find. She hit the button with practiced aim, and for a long moment lay still, listening to the silence that replaced the ringing, a silence that felt, somehow, louder than the alarm had been. （读后续写·清晨起床·日常感与心境描写）

When the first drops of rain began to darken the dusty ground, the oldest farmer in the village climbed to the bell tower and sounded the alarm — not with panic but with the weary authority of a man who had read the sky for sixty years and had never been wrong about a storm. （读后续写·预警·长者智慧）

The cat, in a moment of feline curiosity that it would never be called upon to justify, brushed against the motion sensor and triggered the alarm — plunging the entire office building into the chaos of flashing lights and a siren that could wake the dead. （读后续写·意外触发·幽默场景）

collocations.translation: 关闭闹钟 / 贪睡模式
collocations.example: He hit snooze three times before dragging himself out of bed — not because he was lazy but because his dream had been so vivid, so impossibly real, that waking up felt less like waking and more like being exiled from a world where everything had finally made sense. （读后续写·赖床·梦境留恋）

synonyms.example: Panic spread through the auditorium faster than the smoke — not because the danger was immediate but because panic, unlike fire, needs no oxygen to burn; it feeds on uncertainty and exhales chaos. （读后续写·群体恐慌·心理描写）
synonyms.usage: 比alarm更强烈，暗示失控和混乱，alarm更偏向预警/担忧

synonyms.example: The sudden knock on the window startled her so badly that she dropped the letter she had been reading — a letter that, as it fluttered to the floor like a wounded bird, revealed just enough of its contents to change everything. （读后续写·突然惊吓·关键信息揭示）
synonyms.usage: 强调突然性的惊吓，瞬间的身体反应

advancedExpressions.expression: alarming adj. 令人惊慌的（修饰事物 an alarming speed）｜ alarmed adj. 感到惊慌的（修饰人 be alarmed）｜ alarmingly adv. 惊人地（rise alarmingly）
advancedExpressions.example: The Amazon rainforest is disappearing at an alarming speed, and the crime rate has risen alarmingly — figures that leave every reader alarmed. 亚马逊雨林正以惊人速度消失，犯罪率也惊人地上升——这些数字让每个读者都感到担忧。（课件三形对照）

advancedExpressions.expression: an alarm clock 闹钟 / a fire alarm 火警(警报) / set the alarm 设定闹钟 / the alarm goes off 警报(闹钟)响起 / raise / sound the alarm 拉响警报、敲响警钟 / a false alarm 虚惊一场 / in alarm 惊恐地
advancedExpressions.example: When the fire alarm went off, everyone rushed out in alarm, only to find it was a false alarm. 火警响起时，人人惊恐地冲了出去，结果却是虚惊一场。（一句串起 fire alarm、go off、in alarm、false alarm 四块）

advancedExpressions.type: 同义表达群·使惊恐（供替换升级）
advancedExpressions.expression: alarm sb = frighten sb = scare sb = startle sb = terrify sb（程度递增：startle 一惊 < alarm/frighten/scare 害怕 < terrify 惊恐万分）
advancedExpressions.example: The sudden noise alarmed / startled / frightened everyone in the hall. 突如其来的响声惊到了大厅里所有人。（写作按惊吓程度择词替换）

advancedExpressions.expression: a small alarm bell went off in the back of sb.'s mind
advancedExpressions.example: A small alarm bell went off in the back of her mind when she saw the door ajar — not loud, not urgent, just a quiet, insistent chime that whispered something was not quite right. She almost ignored it. Almost. And the 'almost' made all the difference, because the decision to listen to that tiny internal alarm, to trust the part of herself that noticed things before her conscious mind could name them, saved her life. （潜意识警报→信任直觉→救命）

advancedExpressions.expression: I feel compelled to sound the alarm regarding ...
advancedExpressions.example: I feel compelled to sound the alarm regarding the deteriorating condition of the sports facilities — not because I wish to be difficult but because I believe that if we address this now, we prevent a far more expensive and dangerous situation from developing. （正式提醒/报告）

sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: The alarm rang with the mechanical cruelty of a device that did not know and did not care that she had slept for less than three hours, that the baby had cried through most of those hours, that the presentation was at eight and she was not ready — was not even close to ready — and that somewhere in the exhaustion-soaked fog of her brain, the thought drifted through, unbidden and unwelcome, that she could not do this, could not keep doing this. And then, as if in response to that thought, her foot hit the cold floor, and then the other foot, and the alarm, still ringing, became not a torment but a testimony — proof that she was still here, still moving, still in the fight. （读后续写·极度疲惫的清晨·闹钟从敌人变见证）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 拟人(mechanical cruelty of a device that did not know) + 重复递进(was not ready, not even close) + 转变(alarm as torment → alarm as testimony) + 结尾三叠(still here, still moving, still in the fight)

sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: I want to begin by saying: do not be alarmed. Not because there is nothing to be alarmed about — there is always something to be alarmed about, if you look hard enough — but because alarm is a state that sharpens perception at the cost of judgment. It helps you see the danger; it does not help you decide what to do about it. So let us acknowledge the concern, name it, look it squarely in the face — and then, having looked, let us turn our attention to solutions. For alarm that produces only panic is wasted energy; alarm that produces action is the beginning of change. （应用文·危机演讲·将恐慌转化为行动）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 先稳后论(Do not be alarmed...not because nothing but because...) + 利弊分析(sharpens perception at cost of judgment) + 转化收束(alarm→panic是浪费, alarm→action是改变)

original_sentence: I like it so much that I still use it as my alarm!

classPractice.answer: is disappearing at an alarming speed

classPractice.note: 课件原题。mind (sb's) doing sth 介意某人做某事，用动名词；my 作动名词逻辑主语；the alarm goes off / sounds / rings 闹钟响。

classPractice.question: 一开前门，警铃就会响。Opening the door will ____ ____ ____ ____.
classPractice.note: 课件原题。set off the alarm 触发／使警报响起；动名词短语 Opening the door 作主语。

classPractice.question: 我太喜欢它了，至今仍把它当作我的闹钟用。I like it so much that I still use it as my ____.
classPractice.note: 课文原句；此处 alarm=alarm clock 闹钟

definitionEn:
(1) n. something that you do or give to help make something successful
(2) n. a sum of money given to a person or organization to help them
(3) n. an item that forms part of a book, magazine, broadcast, etc.

uncommonMeanings.meaning: ①捐款，捐赠（可数，a contribution to/toward sth）
uncommonMeanings.example: Every contribution, however small, helps the flood victims rebuild their homes. 每一笔捐款，无论多小，都能帮助水灾灾民重建家园。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: ②（为报刊、书籍等写的）稿件
uncommonMeanings.example: Her contribution to the school magazine was a single paragraph — just one paragraph, tucked between the sports report and the lunch menu — but it was a paragraph about loneliness that named something every teenager in the school had felt and none had dared to speak aloud. And in the weeks that followed, more paragraphs appeared, from more students, until the magazine became not a publication but a conversation. （读后续写·一个段落的涟漪·表达的力量）

readingExamples: I could not make a great contribution because sometimes I wasn't able to express myself clearly in English.

posExamples.sentence: His contribution to the project was invisible to most — he was not the one presenting, not the one whose name appeared on the title page — but without the hours he had spent in the archives, without the data he had painstakingly verified, without the quiet genius of his behind-the-scenes labor, the project would have been, at best, a beautiful house built on sand. （读后续写·幕后英雄·无名贡献的重量）
Every contribution, no matter how small, helps us move closer to our fundraising goal — because a mountain, as the proverb says, is made of pebbles, and a river of raindrops. （应用文·募捐呼吁·积少成多）

wordForms.verb: contribute（vt./vi. 贡献；捐献；投稿；contribute to 导致/促成/为……做贡献）
wordForms.other: 词族全家桶：动词 contribute — 名词 contribution / contributor — 形容词 contributory。核心用法 contribute to sth：①做贡献②捐助③投稿④（贬）导致、促成（Smoking contributes to lung cancer. 吸烟导致肺癌）；名词形式 make a contribution to（to 均为介词，后接名词/动名词）

idioms.example: She made a contribution to the field that was not flashy — no prizes, no headlines, no keynote speeches — but it was the kind of contribution that built the foundation upon which flashier discoveries would later stand, and she was content with that, for she had not entered the field to be known but to know. （读后续写·学者的低调贡献·知识追求）

collocations.phrase: make a huge / major / positive / significant / important contribution (to)
collocations.translation: 【课件】做出巨大／重大／积极／重要的贡献（to sth 对……）
collocations.example: Marie Curie made a great contribution to human development. 玛丽·居里为人类发展做出了巨大的贡献。（课件例句）

collocations.phrase: be a great contribution to sb/sth
collocations.example: The invention of paper is a great contribution to humans. 纸的发明是对人类的一大贡献。（课件例句）

collocations.phrase: make / offer a contribution to charity
collocations.translation: 【课件】给慈善事业捐款（cn. 捐款；un. 捐资这一行为）
collocations.example: All contributions will be gratefully received. 我们对所有的捐资表示感谢。（课件例句）
As a senior high school student, I propose that we (should) make a small contribution to saving wildlife. 作为一名高中生，我提议我们应该为拯救野生动物做出小小贡献。（课件例句）

collocations.translation: 【课件】(v.) 把……捐给／贡献给……；促成、有助于……
collocations.example: She contributed all her pocket money to the earthquake fund. 她把所有的零花钱都捐给了地震基金。／ Plenty of fresh air contributes to good health. 充足的新鲜空气有利于健康。（课件例句）

collocations.translation: 【课件】一个起作用的因素（= 是造成某事的原因之一）
collocations.example: Human error may be a contributing factor. 人为过错可能是一个起作用的因素。（课件例句）
I hope everyone will contribute to the discussion. 我希望大家能参与讨论。（课件例句）

collocations.phrase: contributor (n.) 投稿人；促成因素；捐助者
collocations.translation: 【课件】投稿人／促成因素／捐助者
collocations.example: Stress is a major contributor to most diseases. 压力是大多数疾病的主要原因。／ He became a regular contributor to the magazine. 他成了这家杂志的固定撰稿人。（课件例句）

collocations.translation: 做出巨大贡献（课文原句词块）
collocations.example: I could not make a great contribution because sometimes I wasn't able to express myself clearly in English. 我没能做出很大贡献，因为有时我无法用英语清楚地表达自己。（课文原句）

His most valuable contribution to the debate was not a point he made but a question he asked — a question so simple that everyone in the room wondered, silently and with some embarrassment, why they had not asked it themselves. （读后续写/应用文·提问的价值·一针见血）

The library was built not by a single wealthy donor but by the financial contributions of three thousand ordinary people — families who gave what they could, not because they had extra but because they understood that a library was not a building; it was a door, and every child who walked through that door walked into a larger world. （应用文·社区募捐·教育的力量）

synonyms.translation: 投入，贡献（尤指意见/想法）
synonyms.example: She valued everyone's input — not as a democratic gesture but because she genuinely believed that the best idea in the room could come from anyone, and her job as a leader was not to have the best idea but to create the conditions in which the best idea could emerge. （应用文·领导力理念·集体智慧）
synonyms.usage: 侧重意见、想法的提供，更口语化

synonyms.example: The donation arrived in a plain envelope with no return address and a note that said only, 'For the music program. Every child deserves a song.' And the amount — modest by any standard — was enough to buy three violins, which, over the next decade, would be played by forty-seven students, one of whom would go on to play in a national orchestra. （读后续写·匿名捐赠·蝴蝶效应）
synonyms.usage: 特指金钱或物品捐赠，contribution更泛

advancedExpressions.type: 语法点·构词法·contribute → contribution → contributor（课件）
advancedExpressions.expression: contribute v. 贡献／捐款／促成 —— contribution n. 贡献、捐款 —— contributor n. 投稿人、促成因素、捐助者；核心搭配 contribute (sth) to sth / make a contribution to sth / a contributing factor
advancedExpressions.example: He contributed regularly to the magazine, and each contribution made him a more valued contributor. 他定期给杂志撰稿，每一篇稿件都让他成为更受重视的撰稿人。（一句串起动词、名词、施动名词三态）

advancedExpressions.type: 语法点·propose that + (should) do 虚拟语气（课件）
advancedExpressions.expression: propose that sb (should) do sth —— propose 后的宾语从句用"(should) + 动词原形"虚拟语气
advancedExpressions.example: As a senior high school student, I propose that we (should) make a small contribution to saving wildlife. 作为一名高中生，我提议我们应该为拯救野生动物做出小小贡献。（课件例句：propose that (should) do）

advancedExpressions.expression: make a contribution to sth 为……做贡献 / contribute to sth 贡献于、导致 / contribute sth to sb 把……捐给 / contribute to a magazine 向杂志投稿 / a major contributor 主要贡献者(捐助者)
advancedExpressions.example: The factory contributes to the local economy but also contributes to pollution. 这家工厂既促进了当地经济，也造成了污染。（同一 contribute to 的褒贬两义对照）

advancedExpressions.type: 语法点·make a contribution to + 名词/动名词（to 是介词）
advancedExpressions.expression: make a contribution to (doing) sth = contribute to (doing) sth；此处 to 为介词，后必接名词或动名词，不接动词原形
advancedExpressions.example: Volunteering makes a great contribution to building a harmonious community. 志愿服务对建设和谐社区大有贡献。（易错点：building 不可写成 build）

advancedExpressions.expression: sb.'s contribution was not the kind that made headlines, but ...
advancedExpressions.example: Her contribution was not the kind that made headlines. No building bore her name; no award recognized her decades of service. But in the lives of the students she had taught — the ones who became teachers themselves, who passed on not just knowledge but a way of being in the world — her contribution multiplied, generation after generation, a ripple that would outlast any headline. （教师→学生→再传递→永恒涟漪）

advancedExpressions.expression: every contribution, however modest, brings us one step closer to ...
advancedExpressions.example: Every contribution, however modest, brings us one step closer to a school where no child goes hungry between breakfast and dinner — not because the problem is small but because the community willing to address it is large. （募捐倡议）

sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: His contribution was not measured in money — there was little of that to give — but in time. Every Saturday for twelve years, he showed up at the community center with a chessboard and a thermos of tea, and he taught anyone who wanted to learn. He taught children whose parents worked double shifts, retirees whose days had grown too quiet, teenagers whose anger had nowhere productive to go. And he asked for nothing in return — not because he was saintly but because he had discovered, somewhere in those twelve years of Saturdays, that the person who benefited most from his contribution was himself. Giving, he had learned, was not an expense of the soul but its nourishment. （读后续写·平凡人的非凡贡献·给予即获得）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 否定定义(not measured in money but in time) + 时间跨度(twelve years, every Saturday) + 受益者三叠(children, retirees, teenagers) + 哲理收束(giving is not expense of soul but nourishment)

sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: I am not asking for a contribution today — at least not the kind you write on a check. I am asking for a contribution of attention. A contribution of a single hour to mentor a younger student. A contribution of patience when the person in front of you is struggling. Because the problems we face — and they are real, and they are daunting — will not be solved by money alone. They will be solved by people who decide, individually and together, that they are not content to observe the world's problems from a safe distance. A contribution, in the end, is not about what you give; it is about what you refuse to ignore. （应用文·演讲·重新定义贡献）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 否定引入(not asking for a contribution of the check-writing kind) + 排比定义(A contribution of attention, an hour, patience) + 核心重定(not about what you give but what you refuse to ignore)

original_sentence: I could not make a great contribution because sometimes I wasn't able to express myself clearly in English.

classPractice.question: 玛丽·居里为人类发展做出了巨大的贡献。Marie Curie ____.
classPractice.answer: made a great contribution to human development
classPractice.note: 课件原题。make a great/huge/major/significant contribution to sth 对……做出巨大贡献；to 为介词，后接名词。

classPractice.question: 纸的发明是对人类的一大贡献。The invention of paper ____.
classPractice.answer: is a great contribution to humans
classPractice.note: 课件原题。be a great contribution to sb/sth 是对……的一大贡献；主语 The invention of paper 为单数，谓语用 is。

classPractice.question: 这个项目将增进两国之间的文化交流。This project will ____.
classPractice.answer: contribute to the cultural exchange between the two countries
classPractice.note: 课件原题。contribute to sth = 促进／增进某事；此处等于 be one of the causes of / help。

classPractice.question: All the money ____ (contribute) will go to the charity fund.
classPractice.note: 课件原题。the money 与 contribute 是被动关系（钱被捐），用过去分词 contributed 作后置定语（= which was contributed）。

classPractice.question: 我没能做出很大贡献，因为有时我无法用英语清楚地表达自己。I could not ____ a great ____ because sometimes I wasn't able to express myself clearly in English.

classPractice.question: Everyone should make a contribution to ____ (protect) our shared planet.
classPractice.note: make a contribution to 中 to 是介词，后接动名词 protecting

classPractice.question: Regular exercise ____ (contribute) greatly to good health, so make it a daily habit.

definitionEn:
(1) adv. used to say that it is good that something happened or is the case; by good luck
(2) adv. in a fortunate manner; luckily; happily
(3) adv. (as a sentence adverb) it is a matter of good fortune that ...
readingExamples: Fortunately, my teachers and classmates were always helpful and gave me lots of encouragement.

posExamples.sentence: The bridge gave way three seconds after the last car crossed — three seconds, the width of a breath, the margin between tragedy and a story that would be told, years later, at family gatherings with the nervous laughter of people who had not, as they drove across, understood how close they had come to never arriving at all. Fortunately. One word, so small, containing an entire alternate universe of what-might-have-been. （读后续写·千钧一发·幸存的重量）

Fortunately, the venue turned out to be available on our backup date — a stroke of luck that, I must honestly admit, owed less to careful planning than to the fact that the previous booking had been cancelled at the very last minute. （应用文·活动通知·诚实幽默）

Some argue that success is nothing but a happy accident; fortunately, history tells a different story, for behind almost every so-called 'lucky break' lies years of quiet, unglamorous preparation that finally met its opportunity. （议论文·努力与运气·驳论）

wordForms.other: 词族：名词 fortune 运气/财富 → 形容词 fortunate 幸运的 → 副词 fortunately 幸运地；加否定前缀 un- 全套反义：unfortunate / unfortunately / misfortune（前缀 mis- 表'坏、错'）。作句首独立状语（sentence adverb）时=幸亏，评论整句，后加逗号

collocations.translation: 【课件】名利（fortune n. 运气；财富）
collocations.example: He gave up a life of fame and fortune to teach in a mountain village. 他放弃了名利，去山村教书。
He made a fortune in real estate. 他在房地产上发了财。（课件 slide 21 原题答案）

collocations.translation: 【课件】n. 不幸，灾祸（前缀 mis- 表'坏、错'）
collocations.example: It was a great misfortune that the ship sank on its very first voyage. 那艘船首航即沉，实属大不幸。

collocations.phrase: have the good fortune to do sth
collocations.example: I have had the good fortune to work with you. 我有幸与你共事。（课件 slide 19）

collocations.translation: 【课件】某人交了好运（= sb has good luck）
collocations.example: Fortune smiled on me. = I have good luck. 我交了好运。（课件 slide 19）

collocations.phrase: be fortunate enough to do sth
collocations.translation: 【课件】有幸做某事（fortunate adj. 幸运的）
collocations.example: I have been fortunate enough to visit many parts of the world as a speaker. 我有幸以演讲者的身份游历世界许多地方。（课件 slide 20）
I was fortunate in having a good teacher. 我很幸运有一位好老师。（课件 slide 20）

collocations.phrase: it is (very) fortunate for sb that ...
collocations.example: It was very fortunate for him that I arrived on time. 对他来说很幸运的是我准时到了。（课件 slide 20）

Fortunately for her — and unfortunately for the committee that had rejected her application — she had kept every rejection letter, and at the ceremony where she received the very award they had once deemed her unworthy of, she read from them, not with bitterness but with the gentle irony of someone who understood that the word 'no' is sometimes just 'not yet' in disguise. （读后续写·逆袭·拒绝信的另一种解读）

collocations.translation: 算是够幸运的（加强语气，常带庆幸/如释重负）
collocations.example: Fortunately enough, the storm changed course during the night, and by dawn the fishing boats that had stayed out too late were bobbing safely back into the harbour, their crews too exhausted to do anything but wave. （读后续写·天气转好·劫后余生）
Fortunately, as it turned out, the wrong turn she had cursed for adding an hour to the journey was the very road that led her past the house where an elderly woman had collapsed alone. （读后续写·因祸得福·反转）
Fortunately, thanks to the generosity of our parent volunteers and the tireless efforts of the student council, we were able to raise the full amount — and then some. （应用文·感谢信/活动总结）

collocations.translation: 对所有相关的人来说都幸运的是
collocations.example: Fortunately for all concerned, the misunderstanding was cleared up before it hardened into a lasting grudge, and the two teams that had nearly come to blows ended the day sharing a table and a laugh. （应用文·活动通知/议论文·和解）

collocations.translation: 十分幸运地（正式书面语加强）
collocations.example: Most fortunately, a passing doctor recognised the symptoms at once and began first aid long before the ambulance, delayed by the evening traffic, finally forced its way through. （读后续写·危急救援·关键人物出场）

collocations.translation: 而幸运的是 / 但幸好（转折衔接）
collocations.example: The map had been useless from the start, and the phone had died an hour ago — but fortunately, the old shepherd they stumbled upon knew every goat-path on the mountain by heart. （读后续写·迷路脱困·转折衔接）

synonyms.example: Luckily, the rain held off until the ceremony was over — though the clouds had been gathering all afternoon, dark and patient, as if they too were waiting for the speeches to end before releasing their applause. （读后续写·天公作美·拟人化描写）
synonyms.usage: 更口语化，与fortunately几乎完全可互换；正式书面（应用文、议论文）里fortunately更稳妥，luckily偏轻松随意

synonyms.translation: 幸运地，谢天谢地地（带感情色彩）
synonyms.example: The long meeting ended mercifully early — the chairperson had lost her voice, which everyone agreed, though they expressed the appropriate sympathies, was the best thing that had happened to the committee all year. （读后续写·会议提前结束·讽刺幽默）
synonyms.usage: 强调从痛苦/无聊/危险中解脱的幸运，带「谢天谢地、总算」的情感；fortunately中性，mercifully更主观、更有语气

synonyms.example: Happily, the misunderstanding was soon put right, and the friendship that had almost been lost over a careless word grew, if anything, closer for having been tested. （读后续写·和好·作句首状语）
synonyms.usage: 作句首状语时=fortunately/luckily，语气更文雅书面；注意happily也可作方式状语（快乐地），fortunately则只表庆幸，不表情绪

advancedExpressions.type: 构词法·fortune 词族（课件 slide 18-21）
advancedExpressions.expression: fortune n. 运气/财富 → fortunate adj. 幸运的 → fortunately adv. 幸运地｜加 un-：unfortunate / unfortunately｜加 mis-：misfortune 不幸；高频搭配：fame and fortune 名利、make a fortune 发财、have the good fortune to do 有幸做、be fortunate enough to do 有幸做、be fortunate in doing、it is fortunate for sb that ...
advancedExpressions.example: Fortunately he made a fortune, but unfortunately his misfortune was that he never had the good fortune to enjoy it. 幸运的是他发了财，不幸的是他从未有幸享受它。（一句串起 fortune 词族）

advancedExpressions.expression: fortune 运气 → fortunate 幸运的 → fortunately 幸运地｜加 un-：unfortunate 不幸的 / unfortunately 不幸地｜加 mis-：misfortune 不幸、灾祸
advancedExpressions.example: Fortunately he passed; unfortunately his best friend did not — such is the mix of fortune and misfortune in every exam. 幸运的是他过了；不幸的是他最好的朋友没过——每场考试都是幸与不幸的交织。（一句同现四个同族词）

advancedExpressions.type: 同义表达群·句首'幸好'（供替换升级）
advancedExpressions.expression: Fortunately, ... = Luckily, ... = Happily, ... = As luck would have it, ... = Thankfully, ...（均置于句首作评注状语，后加逗号）
advancedExpressions.example: Fortunately / Luckily / Thankfully, help arrived just in time. 幸好，援助及时赶到。（读后续写转危为安可轮换）

advancedExpressions.expression: Fortunately, as it turned out, ...
advancedExpressions.example: Fortunately, as it turned out, the road she had taken by mistake — the one she had cursed under her breath for adding an hour to her journey — was the road that led past the house where an old woman was having a heart attack, alone, with no one to call for help. And the young woman who had been so angry about the wrong turn became, in that very moment, the right person in the right place at the right time. （错误的转弯→最幸运的偶然→成为别人的救星）

advancedExpressions.expression: Fortunately, thanks to ..., we were able to ...
advancedExpressions.example: Fortunately, thanks to the generosity of our parent volunteers and the tireless efforts of the student council, we were able to raise the full amount — and then some — proving once again that when this community comes together, the word 'impossible' starts to look a lot like 'not yet.' （感谢信/活动总结）

advancedExpressions.expression: What looks like fortune is, more often than not, ...
advancedExpressions.example: What looks like fortune is, more often than not, preparation wearing a lucky disguise; fortunately, the harder we work, the more of these 'lucky breaks' seem to find their way to our door. （辩证观点·把「运气」重新定义为「有准备的机遇」）

sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Fortunately. It is a word we use casually, almost carelessly, to describe the umbrella we remembered on a rainy day or the bus that arrived just as we reached the stop. But sometimes — rarely, terribly — fortunately is the only word standing between a story and a eulogy. It was fortunately that the rope held for four more seconds; fortunately that the search team decided, against protocol, to check one more room; fortunately that a stranger, acting on an instinct she could not explain, chose a different street to walk home. We were saved — not by heroism, not by design, but by a chain of tiny fortunes that, looked at from the right angle, resembled nothing so much as grace. （读后续写·反思「fortunately」的真正含义·凡人恩典）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 对比(umbrella on rainy day vs rope held for four seconds) + 排比三叠(fortunately that...) + 核心比喻(chain of tiny fortunes that resembled grace)

sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: I stand before you today not to claim credit for our success — for success, I have learned, is a mosaic made of many hands — but to acknowledge, with genuine humility, how fortunate we have been. Fortunately, the weather cooperated. Fortunately, the volunteers showed up in numbers we had not dared to hope for. Fortunately, the thousand small things that could have gone wrong — and usually do — chose, this time, to go right. But let us not mistake fortune for strategy. The lesson I take from this is not that we should rely on luck but that we should prepare so thoroughly that fortune, when it comes, has something to work with. （应用文·活动总结演讲·幸运与准备的辩证）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 排比(Fortunately...三次) + 转折(let us not mistake fortune for strategy) + 哲理收束(prepare so thoroughly that fortune has something to work with)

original_sentence: Fortunately, my teachers and classmates were always helpful and gave me lots of encouragement.

classPractice.type: 语境应用·单句语法填空（课件 slide 18）
classPractice.question: I got stuck in the traffic jam, but ____ (fortunate) I arrived on time.
classPractice.note: 修饰整句、表转折的评注状语用副词 fortunately '幸亏、幸运的是'

classPractice.type: 语境应用·完成句子（课件 slide 21 原题①）
classPractice.question: 今年夏天我有幸被邀请去参观上海。This summer I ____ ____ ____ ____ ____ ____ ____ to visit Shanghai.（n. 有幸被邀请）
classPractice.answer: had the good fortune to be invited
classPractice.note: have the good fortune to do 有幸做某事；此处'被邀请'用被动不定式 to be invited

classPractice.type: 语境应用·单句填空（课件 slide 21 原题②）
classPractice.question: Think of those less ____ than yourselves, and you will feel happy.
classPractice.note: less 后接形容词原级，用 fortunate '幸运的'；意为'想想那些不如你幸运的人'

classPractice.type: 语境应用·完成句子（课件 slide 21 原题③）
classPractice.question: 他在房地产上发了财。He ____ ____ ____ in real estate.
classPractice.note: make a fortune 发财、赚大钱；fortune 此处作可数名词'一大笔财富'

classPractice.type: 语境应用·一句多译（课件 slide 21 原题④）
classPractice.question: 她很幸运有份好工作。（用 fortunate 一句多译，写出三种）
classPractice.answer: She is very fortunate in having / to have a good job. / She is very fortunate that she has a good job. / It's very fortunate that she has a good job.
classPractice.note: be fortunate in doing / be fortunate to do / be fortunate that + 从句 / it is fortunate that + 从句，四种句式同义互换

classPractice.question: 幸运的是，我的老师和同学总是乐于助人，给了我很多鼓励。____, my teachers and classmates were always helpful and gave me lots of encouragement.
classPractice.note: 课文原句；Fortunately 置于句首作评注状语，首字母大写，后加逗号

classPractice.question: ____ (fortunate), the storm changed course during the night and the boats returned safely.
classPractice.note: 修饰整句需用副词 fortunately，作句首状语

classPractice.question: ____ (Fortunately / Unfortunately), the ticket was sold out, so we had to change our plans.
classPractice.note: 由结果'票售罄、被迫改计划'判断为不利，用反义 unfortunately

translation: 随着时间流逝，久而久之
definitionEn:
(1) phr. gradually
(2) phr. as time passes
(3) phr. during a period of time
readingExamples: My language skills improved over time.

posExamples.sentence: Over time, the pain did not disappear — pain, she learned, rarely disappears — but it changed shape, softened at the edges, became less a wound and more a scar, something that marked her without defining her. （读后续写·时间治愈·从伤口到伤疤）

Over time, I have come to appreciate that the best learning happens not in the moments of understanding but in the long, frustrating stretches between confusion and clarity — because it is in those stretches that the real work of education takes place. （应用文·学习反思·成长观）

wordForms.other: 辨析小贴士(易混时间短语一网打尽)：over time 随着时间推移、久而久之（强调渐变过程）；on time 准时、按时（不早不晚）；in time 及时、来得及（+ for sth / to do）；at times 有时、间或（=sometimes）；ahead of time 提前。同义替换：as time goes by, with the passage of time, gradually

collocations.translation: 【课件】随着时间流逝；久而久之（强调渐变过程）
collocations.example: My language skills improved over time. 我的语言能力随着时间的推移逐渐提高了。（课件 slide 22 词条主句；引出下方 time 短语群）

collocations.phrase: from time to time / at times
collocations.example: These food safety scares happen from time to time / at times. 这类食品安全恐慌事件时有发生。（课件 slide 22 原题答案）
We'll be there in no time. 我们马上就到。（课件 slide 22 原题答案）

collocations.translation: 【课件】决不，从不（置于句首引起部分倒装）
collocations.example: At no time did anyone involved speak to the press. 任何相关人员都从未向媒体发表过言论。（课件 slide 22；at no time 提前，句子部分倒装 did anyone speak）
That's all my queries for the time being. 眼下我的问题就这些。（课件 slide 23）
This is one of the most-loved Christmas movies of all time. 这是有史以来最受喜爱的圣诞电影之一。（课件 slide 23）
The train arrived ahead of time, but the bus was behind time. 火车提前到了，但公交车晚点了。（课件 slide 23）
She was excited about the trip, but at the same time she felt a little nervous. 她对这次旅行很兴奋，但同时又有点紧张。（课件 slide 23）

collocations.translation: 随着时间发展/变化/改善
collocations.example: Their friendship developed over time — not in the dramatic way of movies, with a single transformative moment, but in the mundane way of real life: through shared lunches, through notes passed in class, through the slow accumulation of small kindnesses that, added together, became something neither of them could imagine living without. （读后续写·友谊的渐进形成·日常的魔力）

Over the course of time, the village changed in ways that were almost imperceptible from one year to the next but unmistakable when you looked back over a generation — the old trees gone, the new roads built, the children who had once played in the square now sending their own children to play in the same square, under different trees. （读后续写·时代变迁·物是人非）

synonyms.example: Gradually — so gradually that she could not have pointed to the exact moment it happened — the language that had once felt like an impenetrable wall became a door. Words that had been strangers became friends; sentences that had been puzzles became pathways; and one day, without ceremony, she realized she was no longer translating in her head but simply understanding, the way you understand the sound of rain. （读后续写·语言习得·从墙到门）
synonyms.usage: 副词，强调变化的渐进性，over time是短语，更灵活

synonyms.example: As time went by, the memory of that terrible day did not fade — as memories are supposed to — but it became less a place she visited daily and more a country she had once lived in, a country whose language she still spoke in dreams but whose streets she no longer walked. （读后续写·创伤记忆·从一个地方到一个国家）
synonyms.usage: 更叙事化，有故事感，适合读后续写

advancedExpressions.type: 短语群·time 时间短语一网打尽（课件 slide 22-23）
advancedExpressions.expression: over time 随时间流逝 / from time to time = at times 有时 / in no time 马上 / at no time 决不（句首倒装）/ for the time being 眼下暂时 / of all time 有史以来 / ahead of time 提前 / behind time 延后 / at the same time = meanwhile 同时 / all the time 一直
advancedExpressions.example: For the time being we practise from time to time, but at no time do we give up, and over time we'll improve — in no time we'll be the best of all time. 眼下我们只是时不时练一练，但我们决不放弃，久而久之定会进步，很快就会成为有史以来最强。（一句串起 time 短语群）

advancedExpressions.type: 同义表达群·时间推移（供替换升级）
advancedExpressions.expression: over time = as time goes / went by = with the passage of time = as the days passed = little by little = gradually（表'随时间渐渐地'，读后续写与议论文可轮换）
advancedExpressions.example: Over time / As time went by / With the passage of time, his skills improved beyond recognition. 随着时间推移，他的技艺进步得判若两人。（三种表达同义替换）

advancedExpressions.type: 语法点·辨析 over/on/in time + at times
advancedExpressions.expression: over time 随时间推移（过程）/ on time 准时（不早不晚）/ in time 及时、来得及（+for/to do）/ at times 有时（=sometimes）
advancedExpressions.example: If you practise over time and arrive on time, you'll be ready in time for the exam — though at times it feels hard. 若你日积月累地练习、准时到场，就能及时为考试做好准备——尽管有时会觉得难。（一句辨清四个短语）

advancedExpressions.expression: over time, what once seemed ... became ...
advancedExpressions.example: Over time, what once seemed like the end of the world became, in retrospect, the beginning of everything that mattered. The rejection from the art school, the breakup she thought would kill her, the failure that had sent her home in disgrace — each of these, over time, revealed itself not as a door closing but as a hand gently turning her toward a door she had not noticed, a door that led, eventually, to a life richer and truer than the one she had originally planned. （苦难→转机→更丰盛的人生）

advancedExpressions.expression: over time, small consistent efforts compound into ...
advancedExpressions.example: Over time, small consistent efforts compound into results that seem, to the outside observer, almost miraculous — but there is no miracle here, only the quiet mathematics of persistence. （建议/演讲·复利效应）

sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Over time — not quickly, not dramatically, not in the way that makes for a good story — he changed. The anger that had defined him for so long, that had cost him jobs and relationships and the trust of people who had once loved him, did not vanish. It eroded. Like a cliff facing the sea, it was worn down not by a single storm but by the daily, patient, relentless work of ordinary life — by the therapist who refused to give up on him, by the dog that needed walking every morning regardless of his mood, by the small child next door who did not know his history and therefore treated him, inexplicably, like someone worth knowing. Over time, the man who had been a cliff became a shore — still shaped by the same forces, but softer, more accessible, a place where things could land and grow. （读后续写·愤怒的侵蚀·悬崖变海岸·时间重塑）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 三副否定(not quickly, not dramatically, not in the way...) + 核心比喻(anger eroded like a cliff facing the sea) + 转折因素(therapist, dog, child) + 意象转换(cliff→shore) + 结尾画面(place where things could land and grow)

sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Over time, things get better — not because time itself has magical healing properties but because time, if you use it well, is the raw material of improvement. A single day of effort is almost invisible; a week is barely noticeable; a month might show a hint of progress. But over time — over a year, over a decade, over a lifetime of showing up and doing the work — the accumulation of those invisible days becomes something unmistakable. So do not be discouraged by the invisibility of today's effort. Trust the process. Trust the accumulation. Trust, above all, the quiet, unglamorous, transformative power of doing a small thing consistently over time. （应用文·演讲·时间的复利力量）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 反驳引入(not because time has magical properties) + 时间递进(day→week→month→year→decade→lifetime) + 三叠祈使(Trust the process. Trust the accumulation. Trust the power.)

original_sentence: My language skills improved over time.

classPractice.type: 语境应用·完成句子（课件 slide 22 原题①）
classPractice.question: 这种食品安全恐慌事件时有发生。These food safety scares happen ____ ____ ____ ____.
classPractice.note: from time to time = at times 有时、时不时；表'间或发生'

classPractice.question: 我们马上就到。We'll be there ____ ____ ____.
